findings.explanation: Only the Client can terminate the agreement without cause under this provision, while you do not have a corresponding right. Because completed work is still paid, this creates a minor imbalance.
findings.suggested_change: Either party may terminate this Agreement upon ninety (90) days prior written notice to the other party.

findings.quoted_text: EXCEPT FOR CLAIMS UNDER SECTION 9 HEREOF, THE      LIABILITY OF A PARTY TO THE OTHER FOR DIRECT DAMAGES SHALL NOT EXCEED      FIFTEEN MILLION DOLLARS.
findings.explanation: Your liability cap excludes Section 9 claims, meaning your indemnification and IP infringement obligations have no limit and expose you to uncapped financial exposure.
findings.suggested_change: The liability of a party to the other for direct damages shall not exceed fifteen million dollars, inclusive of all claims under Section 9 hereof.

findings.quoted_text: $2,000,000 on or before           September 30, 1998, and the balance within sixty (60) days of the           execution of this Agreement.
findings.explanation: Payment is delayed to 60 days, which exceeds standard 30-day payment terms and impacts your cash flow.
findings.suggested_change: The balance shall be payable within thirty (30) days of the execution of this Agreement.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hello. I hope this email finds you well. Before signing the agreement, I would like to propose a couple of adjustments: - Regarding the liability provisions in the relevant clause, the current terms leave certain claims uncapped; I propose updating this so that the liability of a party to the other for direct damages shall not exceed fifteen million dollars, inclusive of all claims under Section 9 hereof. - Regarding the payment terms in the agreement, the 60-day timeline impacts cash flow; I propose updating the text so that the balance shall be payable within thirty days of the execution of this agreement. Thank you for your time and consideration.
